title: Platform incident statemachine catalog and decision runbook
author: Priya Nambiar
body:
Summary:
This runbook catalogs the canonical incident statemachines we use across the platform and provides a compact decision-runbook for operators. The goal: reduce cognitive load during multi-signal degradations by prescribing state transitions, deterministic actions, and automation hooks that preserve SLOs while minimizing customer impact.

Scope and intended audience:
- Scope: multi-tenant inference platform services (request router, batching service, KV prefix cache, model runtime pool, allocator).
- Audience: platform operators, oncall engineers, platform SREs, and automation engineers writing state transition tests.

Why this exists:
1) Operators often see multiple conflicting signals (latency, error-rate, cost-surge) — a statemachine forces a canonical interpretation and action set.
2) Playbooks for each state reduce ad-hoc interventions and speed recovery.

Key definitions:
- State: high-level classification of service health (OK, WarmDegraded, ColdDegraded, Congested, Evicting, Fallbacking, Recovering).
- Trigger: measurable telemetry that causes a transition (e.g., 95th percentile token-latency > 2000ms for 3m).
- Action: concrete operator or automated steps.

Responsibility matrix:
- Primary oncall: Triage + initial mitigation.
- Platform-operator-runbook-owner: Coordinates canaries, escalations, and permanent fixes.
- Automation-team: Maintains automation hooks and tests for statemachine transitions.

Statemachine catalog (summary table):
| State Name | Typical triggers (examples) | Immediate operator action (first 5 min) | Automation hook |
|------------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------|-----------------|
| OK | All SLOs within tolerance | Monitor | none |
| WarmDegraded | 95p latency 500-1200ms for 5m; small error-rate bump | Apply warmset prefretch, reduce batching window by 10% | prefetch-policy api/v1/hint | 
| ColdDegraded | 95p latency 1200-2500ms for 3m + KV cache-miss rate > 40% | Increase prefix-cache replica, enable aggressive warmup; mark affected pools | cache-replicator job | 
| Congested | CPU/GPU utilization >= 92% across pool for 2m and request queue length growth > 20% | Apply tenant-shed policy for burst-credited tenants; open emergency burst capacity | tenant-shed service call | 
| Evicting | Persistent preemptions or thermal-shutdown risk | Drain low-priority pools, move critical traffic to dedicated fallback models | allocator-drain api | 
| Fallbacking | Model failures or degraded output quality detectors firing | Route to validated fallback variant (quantized / smaller model) with score-preservation | routing-policy /fallbacks | 
| Recovering | All critical signals trending back to normal for 10m | Gradual rollback of mitigations, monitor for regressions | orchestrator rollout API | 

Note: thresholds above are example triggers. Refer to SLI mapping table below for precise metrics per service.

SLI-to-state mapping (condensed):
- Latency SLI (95p token latency): WarmDegraded (500-1200ms) -> ColdDegraded (1200-2500ms) -> Congested/Evicting (>2500ms or long tail growth).
- Error SLI (5xx rate): >0.5% sustained => investigate runtime errors -> Fallbacking if model-level errors.
- Cache SLI (prefix cache miss rate): >30% => WarmDegraded; >50% => ColdDegraded.

Operator decision flow (quick checklist):
1) Confirm alarms: verify dashboards and check correlated signals (queue length, host GPU temp, eviction events, allocator metrics).
2) Classify state according to SLI-to-state mapping.
3) Execute immediate operator actions from the catalog table.
4) If mitigation is automated, confirm automation executed and verify outcome for 3 monitoring windows (3 x 1 minute).
5) If automation failed or the signal worsened, escalate to P1 RT (follow escalation page).
6) Begin rollback plan when Recovering state maintained for 10 minutes.

Detailed runbook examples (templates):
A) ColdDegraded (KV cache miss spike due to metadata inconsistency)
- Symptoms: cache-miss rate > 50%, 95p latency up 40–1500ms, increase in cold-starts in logs.
- Immediate steps (0-5m):
  1. Run `kubectl -n platform exec -it cache-replicator-0 -- /bin/sh -c "curl -sf http://localhost/health"` to check liveness.
  2. Trigger cache replica scaling: `POST /api/v1/cache/replicas {"replicas": 3, "reason": "ops:ColdDegraded"}`.
  3. Run targeted prefix warmup for top-50 tenants: `scripts/warmup-prefixes --tenants-file /tmp/top50.csv`.
  4. Annotate incident: add to timeline with tags `statemachine:ColdDegraded` and `mitigation:cache-replicas`.
- Follow-up steps (5-30m):
  1. Monitor key metrics: cache-miss, 95p latency, cold-starts per minute.
  2. If no improvement in 10m, increase replicas by +2 and open allocator inspector.
- Post-incident: run eviction-simulation test to validate allocation heuristics and create bug for root cause.

B) Congested (allocator saturation due to bursty tenant)
- Symptoms: GPU util > 92%, request backlog doubling in 2m, tenant burst credits consumed.
- Immediate steps (0-10m):
  1. Identify top tenants by tail latency: query `SELECT tenant_id, p95_latency FROM metrics WHERE window=5m ORDER BY p95_latency DESC LIMIT 10`.
  2. Apply soft-shed to top non-critical tenants: `POST /ops/tenant-shed {"tenants": [..], "percentage": 30}`.
  3. Notify capacity-team channel with payload containing tenant list and metrics snapshot.
- Follow-up: If congestion persists, enable burst capacity in region (if available) or initiate cross-region failover routing.

Automation hooks and safety checks:
- Every automated mitigation must emit an event to `platform.events.statetransitions` with fields: timestamp, previous_state, new_state, automation_id, operator_id (if manual).
- Safety check examples:
  - Automation to increase cache replicas should abort if node thermal alarm present.
  - Tenant-shed automation will never exceed defined per-tenant hard limit (see config table).

Configuration reference (operator-facing table):
| Config key | Default | Operator override method | Notes |
|------------|---------|-------------------------|-------|
| cache.replicas.max | 12 | POST /api/v1/cache/replicas | Global safety ceiling |
| allocator.eviction.threshold | 0.92 | POST /api/v1/allocator/evict | Fraction of GPU util to trigger evictions |
| routing.fallback.priority | high | /admin/routing | Determines which tenants get fallback first |

Monitoring checklist (dashboard links and queries):
- Primary dashboards: Platform -> Inference -> StateTransitions overview (link: /dashboards/platform/inference/state-transitions)
- Quick queries:
  1. Recent state transitions: `logs | where event="state_transition" | sort by timestamp desc | limit 50`
  2. Top 10 tenants by 95p latency: see Congested section above.

Escalation and communications:
1) If state escalates to Evicting or Fallbacking and lasts > 15 minutes, open an incident and set priority P1.
2) Use incident template: include affected tenants, duration, mitigation actions, and customer-impact estimate (tokens/min lost).
3) Notifying channels: #platform-oncall, #capacity-team, and customer-success for named customers (if confidentiality required use restricted template).

Simulation & verification playbook (gameday recipe):
- Objective: validate statemachine correctness and automation safety without impacting production traffic.
- Steps:
  1. Create a synthetic tenant in canary cluster with configurable burst behavior.
  2. Inject 95p latency and cache miss signals using the synthetic workload generator.
  3. Verify system transitions from OK -> WarmDegraded -> ColdDegraded and automation responses.
  4. Confirm automation emits events and rollback occurs when signals subside.
  5. Post-sim retro: capture operator decisions, time-to-mitigation, and any manual overrides.

Retrospective and continuous improvement checklist:
- After each runbook invocation record:
  - Time to classification, time to first action, time to visible improvement.
  - Any gaps in dashboards or missing telemetry.
  - False-positive triggers (tweak thresholds).
- Quarterly: run a focused simulation on at least 3 statemachines and publish a short retrospective with action items.

Appendix: common commands and snippets
- Force a state transition (operator-only, uses RBAC):
  `curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://ops.internal/api/v1/states/transition -d '{"service":"inference-router","target_state":"WarmDegraded","reason":"ops:test"}'`
- Inspect most recent automation event:
  `curl https://telemetry.internal/api/events?type=state_transition&limit=1 | jq .`

Related pages and references:
- See platform incident automation SLA (link: /eng-platform/systems-and-services/operator-automation-and-sla-2026)
- See canary cluster synthetic workload generator docs (link: /eng-platform/runbooks/synthetic-scenario-orchestrator-runbook-2026)

Ownership and maintenance cadence:
- Runbook owner: platform-operator-runbook-owner (rotating role).
- Review cadence: every 6 months or after any P1 involving state transitions.

Contact and support:
- Oncall escalation: #platform-oncall -> PagerDuty rotation (platform-sre)
- Automation questions: automation-team@redwood.com

Document history:
- 2025-11-12: Created by Priya Nambiar
- 2026-01-20: Added Congested/Evicting states and tenant-shed templates (review: Ethan Chen)

End of document.
